- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is rising steadily, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after recent spikes.  
- If official event net is bearish (supply_net < 0) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for supply pressure.  
- If sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33) and forecast is rising, apply downward bias to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (true outcome > 70), model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish signals (≥3 consecutive 0.33 or lower), model should not assume continuation of upward trend — apply mean reversion bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >15% from 18-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent mean reversion trend.  
- When multiple auction events (supply_net < 0) occur within 7 days, forecast should be capped at 10–15% below historical high of 18-day window.
